source.title: Restore the Array From Adjacent Pairs

teaching.hint: What can the number of neighbors of a value reveal about its position in the array?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The unordered pairs form one simple path whose two endpoints have one neighbor each.
solution_outline.approach: Build neighbors for each value, begin at either one-neighbor endpoint, and repeatedly take the neighbor that is not the previous value.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The current and previous values identify a unique forward edge on a degree-at-most-two path; the output prefix is a valid prefix of one orientation of the hidden array.
solution_outline.correctness: Every supplied pair is exactly an edge of the original array’s path. The forced walk from an endpoint visits every unique value once and uses every edge; either direction is accepted.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) expected time and O(n) space for adjacency and output.
solution_outline.pitfall: Starting from an interior value can branch into two directions and omit part of the path.

common_wrong_turns: Assume pair order or orientation matches the array
Start from a degree-two value without a path direction
source_fidelity_notes: Kept uniqueness, arbitrary pair orientation and order, and acceptance of either reconstruction direction.
